# PulsHealth

> Sync Apple Health data from an iPhone to a backend you run, then use it with your own tools — SQL, Grafana, notebooks and AI assistants. An iOS app and the Swift package under it read HealthKit and stream every sample as gzip NDJSON to an HTTP endpoint you configure; the repository also ships a reference backend (PostgreSQL 17 + TimescaleDB, a Go ingest server, a read-only Go product API with OpenAPI, Grafana dashboards, a Next.js viewer and an MCP server) and the open sync protocol, so anyone can write their own receiver. Apache-2.0. The iOS app is free on the App Store (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/pulshealth/id6757657354); the self-hosted backend is pre-release. Site: https://pulshealth.com. Source: https://github.com/PulsHealth/pulshealth

Dates on the wire are epoch milliseconds; every quantity type has one canonical unit; daily values are deduplicated across an iPhone and an Apple Watch, raw samples deliberately are not. Read `docs/database-guide.md` before drawing a conclusion from the data.

## Get it

- The iOS app: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/pulshealth/id6757657354 — free, iPhone. It needs a backend of your own to sync to; `README.md` brings one up with one command.
- The website: https://pulshealth.com — what the app does, the HealthKit knowledge base, the blog, and the project documentation rendered from this repository at https://pulshealth.com/docs/. Its source is `site/` in this repository.

## Start here

- [README.md](README.md): what the project is, the component table, and the one-command quickstart for the server and the app.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): orientation for an automated contributor — components, where the authoritative facts live, the invariants, and how to run each test suite.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): the deep guide — the invariants in full, with the reasoning, and the gotchas (HealthKit crashes, iOS permission bugs, TimescaleDB compression traps).
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): sign-off (DCO, no CLA), code style, and what a pull request must carry.

## The protocol

- [docs/protocol/README.md](docs/protocol/README.md): the Puls Sync Protocol v1 specification, written for receiver implementers. Rendered at https://pulshealth.com/docs/protocol/.
- [docs/protocol/catalog.json](docs/protocol/catalog.json): the published type vocabulary — every HealthKit identifier with its kind, canonical unit and legal aggregate functions. Generated from the Swift catalog; never hand-edited.
- [docs/protocol/catalog.md](docs/protocol/catalog.md): what the catalog's fields mean and how it is regenerated.
- [examples/receivers/python-sqlite/README.md](examples/receivers/python-sqlite/README.md): a complete third-party receiver in standard-library Python.

## The data

- [docs/database-guide.md](docs/database-guide.md): the authoritative guide to the schema — every table family, what each column means, which table answers which question, and the traps (device double counting above all). Rendered at https://pulshealth.com/docs/database/.
- [docs/export.md](docs/export.md): bulk export of a whole range as streamed CSV or JSONL, over `GET /v1/export` or the `puls-export` CLI — and, with no server at all, from the app's Export tab. Rendered at https://pulshealth.com/docs/export/.
- [server/README.md](server/README.md): running the reference backend — Compose services, environment, schema migrations, the ingest wire format and the product API. Rendered at https://pulshealth.com/docs/server/.

## AI assistants

- [docs/ai.md](docs/ai.md): connecting Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor or a ChatGPT Action to your own data, and what each tool answers. Rendered at https://pulshealth.com/docs/ai/.
- [server/mcp/README.md](server/mcp/README.md): the MCP server itself — transports, configuration and its security model.

## Optional

- [server/api/docs.go](server/api/docs.go): the OpenAPI 3.1 document for the product API, served live at `/openapi.json` with an HTML reference at `/docs`.
- [web/README.md](web/README.md): the Next.js viewer.
- [PulsHealthSync/README.md](PulsHealthSync/README.md): the Swift sync package — architecture, wire format and performance numbers.
- [PulsHealth/README.md](PulsHealth/README.md): the iOS app.
- [site/README.md](site/README.md): the marketing site behind pulshealth.com — a Next.js static export built with bun, distinct from the self-hosted viewer in `web/`.
- [knowledge-base/README.md](knowledge-base/README.md): the 178 YAML files behind the site's HealthKit type pages — clinical prose, ranges and sources, one per type.
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): how to report a vulnerability, which versions are supported, and the design properties to know about.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each release of the server stack, and which versions are tracked elsewhere.
- [docs/roadmap.md](docs/roadmap.md): what is still outstanding, in the order worth doing it, with the requirement IDs from the plan behind it, and what was decided against.
